hook: Anima Anandkumar is a computer scientist known for pioneering the use of tensor decomposition methods to give provable guarantees for learning latent variable models, an alternative to techniques that lacked theoretical grounding. She earned a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Madras in 2004 and a PhD in electrical and computer engineering from Cornell University in 2009, followed by a postdoctoral position at MIT. She then built an academic career at the University of California, Irvine, rising from assistant to associate professor, before moving into industry as a principal scientist at Amazon AI and later as director and then senior director of AI research at NVIDIA. Since 2017 she has held the Bren Professorship in Computing and Mathematical Sciences at Caltech, where her group extends foundational machine learning theory into applied problems such as physics informed neural networks, weather forecasting and drug discovery. Her career bridges rigorous theoretical work on learning algorithms with large scale applied AI research built inside major technology companies.

Pioneered tensor decomposition methods that provide theoretical guarantees for learning latent variable models

Bren Professor of Computing and Mathematical Sciences at Caltech since 2017
Fellow of IEEE (2020) and ACM (2022), and a Guggenheim Fellow (2023)
Research applies machine learning methods to scientific problems including weather forecasting and physics simulation
